title: chore: Add APNS content_available and mutable_content to FCM messages
body:
Closes #16

## Problem

Data-only FCM messages (no `notification` field) are silently dropped on iOS when the app is killed or suspended. Without `content-available` and `mutable-content` in the APNS payload, iOS has no reason to wake the app or route the notification through the Notification Service Extension.

## Why this approach

The root cause is that `Message::Token` was constructed with `apns: None` in `RealFcmClient::send_single()` — the single point where Firebase messages are built. Fixing it here means every outgoing message automatically gets the correct APNS config, with no opt-in required per notification type.

APNS config was placed in `fcm_sender.rs` (transport layer) rather than in `FcmPayload`/`event_handler.rs` because: (1) all our messages need these flags, (2) the typed `ApnsConfig` API from `firebase-messaging-rs` is cleaner than the `serde_json::Value` that `FcmPayload.apns` uses, and (3) it keeps event handling decoupled from iOS delivery mechanics.

Two code paths based on message content:
- **Alert path** — messages with title/body get a `RichAlert` in `aps.alert`, plus `content-available: 1` and `mutable-content: 1`, with `apns-push-type: alert` and priority 10. Title/body are filtered from custom data to avoid duplication with `aps.alert`.
- **Background path** — data-only messages without title/body use `ios_background_notification()` which sets `content-available: 1` with background push type and priority 5.

A `debug_assert!` guards against future code accidentally setting `FcmPayload.apns`, enforcing that APNS config is transport-owned.

## Trade-offs

- **Android unaffected** — FCM ignores the `apns` field for Android devices.
- **Requires iOS Notification Service Extension** — the diVine iOS app must have one to leverage `mutable-content`. Assumed already in place.
- **No per-message opt-out** — every message gets the APNS override. Intentional since all messages are data-only and need background delivery.

## Test plan

- `test_build_apns_config_creates_alert_payload_from_data_only_message` — verifies alert path JSON structure
- `test_build_apns_config_uses_background_transport_without_alert_fields` — verifies background path JSON structure
- All existing tests pass, clippy clean

title: chore: Remove test environment from CI deploy dispatch
body:
Closes #14

## Summary

The `repository_dispatch` payload to `divine-iac-coreconfig` includes `"test"` in the environments array, but the test ArgoCD cluster (`argocd.test.dvines.org`) is unreachable. This causes the downstream post-merge-sync job to fail on every deploy, blocking production promotion.

Removes `"test"` from both conditional branches in the deploy job's "Determine environments" step so the dispatch only targets reachable clusters.

## Trade-offs

- The docker "Push to Test" step and its summary line are intentionally kept — those push images to the test registry but don't trigger ArgoCD sync. A separate IAC issue will coordinate broader test environment removal.
- The `divine-push-service` ApplicationSet in IAC doesn't target the test environment, so there is no functional impact beyond unblocking deploys.

## Test plan

- [x] Verified the change is limited to the two environment arrays
- [ ] Trigger a non-tag push and confirm the dispatch payload no longer includes `"test"`
- [ ] Trigger a tag push and confirm `"test"` is absent from the production-path payload

title: docs: Return JSON with pubkey from health endpoint
body:
Closes #10

Changed the health endpoint to return JSON `{"status": "ok", "pubkey": "<hex>"}` instead of plain text "OK", so the mobile app can discover the push service pubkey per environment without hardcoding it. K8s probes are unaffected — they only check the HTTP status code. Pubkey is null if no service key is configured.

title: Update NIP draft to match simplified push service model
body:
## Summary

- Remove Kind 3081/3082 (dynamic filter upsert/delete) from the NIP draft -- these were from the old generic nostr-push-service and are not implemented
- Add Kind 3083 (notification preferences) as optional -- lets users control which event kinds they receive notifications for
- Simplify notification triggers section -- services define their own triggers with hardcoded filters, no client-side filter management needed

The NIP now matches what divine-push-service actually implements: 3079 (register), 3080 (deregister), and optionally 3083 (preferences).

title: Rewrite CI for Artifact Registry and add ADC support for GKE deployment
body:
## Summary

- Rewrite CI workflow to push images to GCP Artifact Registry via Workload Identity
  Federation (matching keycast/funnelcake deploy pattern), replacing the old GHCR-based flow
- Remove dead code: `get_version`, `merge_to_release` (referenced non-existent Helm charts)
- Make Firebase `credentials_path` optional to support Application Default Credentials
  (ADC) via GKE Workload Identity, eliminating the need for service account JSON files

Since the service runs on GKE, it no longer needs manually provisioned Firebase
credentials — Workload Identity provides them automatically via ADC. The
`credentials_path` config option is kept for local development but is now optional.

## Changes

- `.github/workflows/publish-and-release.yml` — full rewrite with per-environment
  push jobs (poc, test, staging, production) and coreconfig dispatch for ArgoCD
- `src/config.rs` — `credentials_path` is now `Option<String>` with `#[serde(default)]`
- `src/state.rs` — only sets `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` when `credentials_path`
  is provided; otherwise logs ADC usage
- `config/settings.yaml` — removed `credentials_path` (production uses ADC)

title: Rewrite CI for build-once pattern and add ADC support
body:
## Description

Rewrite the CI workflow to match the build-once pattern used by keycast and
funnelcake: build the Docker image once, then push to each GCP Artifact
Registry environment via `docker-push-gcp@v1`, avoiding the SLSA attestation
bug that blocks `build-push-action` direct pushes. Also makes
`credentials_path` optional so the service can use Application Default
Credentials on GKE (Workload Identity), and adds a pubkey allowlist for
restricting notifications in non-production environments.

## Type of Change

- [x] Code refactor
- [x] Build configuration change

## Dependencies

- divinevideo/divine-iac-coreconfig#313 must merge first (adds
  `divine-push-service` to the image-deploy and post-merge-sync workflow
  allowlists)

title: divine-push-service#4: Fix dedup race condition for multi-replica safety
body:
Closes #4

## Summary

Fixes a dedup race condition where multiple replicas could both send push notifications for the same event. The old two-step pattern (SISMEMBER then SADD) had a window where concurrent replicas could both read "not processed" before either marked the event.

## Changes

- **`src/redis_store.rs`**: Replace `is_event_processed()` + `mark_event_processed()` with a single `try_claim_event()` that uses `SET NX EX` - atomic set-if-not-exists with per-key TTL
- **`src/redis_store.rs`**: Remove `PROCESSED_EVENTS_SET` constant (shared set no longer used)
- **`src/event_handler.rs`**: Replace check-then-mark pattern with a single `try_claim_event()` call before processing, removing the post-processing mark step entirely

## Decisions

- **`SET NX EX` over `SADD`**: The issue suggested SADD-based atomicity, but SET NX EX is fully atomic (set + TTL in one command) vs SADD + EXPIRE which is still two operations
- **Per-event keys (`dedup:<event_id>`) over shared set**: Fixes the secondary bug where EXPIRE on the shared set was resetting TTL for all events on every insertion. Each key now has independent TTL
- **Claim-before-process**: If processing fails after claiming, the event won't retry for TTL duration. This is an acceptable tradeoff vs duplicate notifications

## Test plan

- [x] All 36 unit tests pass
- [x] Clippy clean
- [ ] Manual test with Redis: verify SET NX EX returns OK on first call, nil on second
- [ ] Follow-up #5 tracks adding integration tests for concurrent dedup scenarios
